objectives: Turn Lifecycle email and deliverability into concrete, measurable decisions that can be applied to a real store.

blocks.text: Orchestrate welcome, cart, order, usage, replenishment, and reactivation based on event, consent, frequency, and real value. A sound decision always connects the customer need, the visual or commercial rule, its implementation in the site, and an observable signal. This prevents vague preferences and copied tactics whose purpose is not understood.

blocks.title: Simple analogy
blocks.text: Lifecycle email and deliverability is like arranging a physical shop: every color, space, message, or offer should help a visitor understand where they are, what they can buy, and why they can trust the next step.

Orchestrate welcome, cart, order, usage, replenishment, and reactivation based on event, consent, frequency, and real value. Name the precise problem before selecting a tool. Observe context, device, intent, and customer objections. Then write a hypothesis that links one change to an expected result without presenting that hypothesis as established fact.

To master Lifecycle email and deliverability, first build a minimal version with explicit rules, then inspect it on mobile and desktop. Contrast normal, empty, long, and error cases. Quality comes from a coherent testable system, not from accumulating visual effects or promotional messages.

This lesson delivers an email lifecycle map with stopping rules. It must record the starting situation, decision, expected evidence, and safety limit. Compare behavior and before/after metrics over enough time while accounting for traffic, costs, and satisfaction.

blocks.text: Read retention by first order, product, channel, and period; complement numbers with qualitative reasons and prioritize controllable causes. A sound decision always connects the customer need, the visual or commercial rule, its implementation in the site, and an observable signal. This prevents vague preferences and copied tactics whose purpose is not understood.

blocks.title: Simple analogy
blocks.text: Cohorts, repeat purchase, churn, and customer voice is like arranging a physical shop: every color, space, message, or offer should help a visitor understand where they are, what they can buy, and why they can trust the next step.

Read retention by first order, product, channel, and period; complement numbers with qualitative reasons and prioritize controllable causes. Name the precise problem before selecting a tool. Observe context, device, intent, and customer objections. Then write a hypothesis that links one change to an expected result without presenting that hypothesis as established fact.

To master Cohorts, repeat purchase, churn, and customer voice, first build a minimal version with explicit rules, then inspect it on mobile and desktop. Contrast normal, empty, long, and error cases. Quality comes from a coherent testable system, not from accumulating visual effects or promotional messages.
